title: Ite, Missa est
notes: The dismissal: the last Dóminus vobíscum of the Mass, the deacon's or priest's Ite, Missa est, and the answer Deo grátias. The missal gives three further dismissals — the Easter form with allelúia, Benedicámus Dómino where a procession follows the Mass (the 1960 Codex n. 507 confined it so), Requiéscant in pace in Masses for the Dead — and they are named in the rubrics at s04 and s07 rather than encoded as words: only the Easter form appears in Latin in the second witness, on its chant page, so the others would rest on one witness alone. ITE at w007 carries no conj: eo is irregular, and SCHEMA.md omits the field for irregular verbs. MISSA at w008 is the noun missa, -æ in the nominative, not the participle of mitto: both analyzers head the noun, and the phrase is the sentence Ite, missa est — go, the dismissal is made. DEO at w010 is dative and GRÁTIAS at w011 accusative plural because the answer is elliptical: the verb agámus (or ago) is understood, as at the Preface dialogue's Grátias agámus Dómino Deo nostro. The rubric at s07 sets Requiéscant with its accent; witness do prints the word unaccented at this one place and accented elsewhere in the same file. VOBÍSCUM at w002 is the pronoun with its enclitic cum; Collatinus dictionaries the fused form as a lemma of its own and tags it singular, which the pipeline sets aside by a recorded ruling — hence the medium confidence and the disputed review, as at ordinarium.praefatio-dialogus w002.

source.method: Verified by collation against the independent witnesses below: zero substantive divergence, and no accidental variant either — the two editions set this dismissal identically.

segments.text: dicit pro Missæ qualitate, vel Ite, Missa est, vel Benedicámus Dómino. Deo grátias.
In Missis Defunctorum dicit: Requiéscant in pace. Amen.
